results.question: Who can get the general social security benefit when they are unemployed?
results.answer:
You may get the general social security benefit if you are unemployed and meet the following criteria:
- You are 18 to 64 years old [S7][S8].
- You live permanently in Finland [S7][S8].
- You are registered as an unemployed jobseeker with the employment services of your municipality of residence [S5][S7][S8].
- You cannot get earnings-related unemployment allowance, or your unemployment fund has already paid it to you for the maximum number of days [S7][S8]. 
Additionally, individuals staying in Finland with a temporary residence permit can get the benefit for a maximum of 400 days if they fulfil the work requirement [S1].

results.question: Is there a waiting period before I can get the general social security benefit?
results.answer:
Yes, you generally must complete a waiting period (*omavastuuaika*) of 7 working days before you can receive the general social security benefit [S2][S4]. 

You register as an unemployed jobseeker with the employment services on your first day of unemployment to start this process [S4]. However, you do not need to complete a new waiting period if you move directly from earnings-related unemployment allowance to the general social security benefit [S2][S5].

results.question: How does part-time work affect my general social security benefit?
results.answer:
You can receive an adjusted general social security benefit while working part-time [S2][S4]. Your earned wages or salary will reduce the amount of your benefit [S5]. As a basic rule, the benefit is reduced by 50 cents for every 1 euro you earn [S8]. 

The income affects the benefit during the specific payment period in which the wages or salary are actually paid to you, regardless of when you earned them [S1][S8]. To qualify, you must stay registered as a jobseeker with employment services and look for full-time work according to your employment plan [S4].

results.question: Can income other than wages reduce my general social security benefit?
results.answer:
Yes, income other than wages or salary can reduce your general social security benefit because the benefit is means-tested [S1][S3]. 

Other income that can reduce your benefit includes capital income, informal care allowances, partial early old-age pensions, compensations for family caregivers, and copyright royalties [S3]. 

If you receive more than €311 per month in capital income or other non-wage income, half of the amount exceeding this limit will be deducted from your benefit [S3][S4]. However, these types of income will not reduce your benefit if you participate in employment-promoting services [S4]. 

Savings, assets, or the income of your partner or roommate do not affect the amount you can get [S3].
